project.title: Purchasing — supplier and purchase request information model

entityTypes.name: Supplier
entityTypes.description: Suppliers from whom the organization buys goods, services or works. Selected on purchase requests and orders so the counterparty's identity, contacts and agreed terms are entered once and reused.
entityTypes.namePattern: Trading name as it appears on quotations and invoices (e.g. «Demonstration Supplies, Lda.»). Add the accounting supplier code only when two suppliers share a name.
entityTypes.purpose: Purchase requests (suggested supplier), purchase orders (counterparty, terms, contact), invoice matching and supplier evaluation.
entityTypes.owner: Purchasing team (assumed; confirm — see decision D2)

coverage.reason: Native Name carries the trading name; legal name, NIF, accounting code and category cover the order header, invoice matching and reporting by category.
The commercial contact receives requests for quotation and orders; address and country are needed on the order and to recognise foreign suppliers.
One relationship owner in Purchasing maintains the record and answers questions about the supplier.

Relationship status distinguishes prospective, active, suspended and closed suppliers before an order is placed; approval date records when qualification happened, if the organization qualifies suppliers.
Currency, payment terms, lead time and framework agreement feed the order and the budget confirmation without re-entry on each request.
Purchase requests and orders reference the supplier from the case (entity field on the workflow). No inverse list is kept on the supplier; Provia shows linked cases from the record.
Bank details, tax certificates and the signed contract stay in the accounting system and document repository; the record holds the accounting code and the agreement link only.
A rating or last-evaluation date needs a defined evaluation process; none was supplied. Added when the evaluation cycle is confirmed (decision D5).

setup: Sources: none supplied. All fields, options and maintainers are assumptions to confirm with Purchasing and Finance.
Native record Name, UUID, creator and timestamps are used as-is; no display-name, source-system or provenance fields are added.
If the destination already has a supplier type, reuse it and reconcile these fields against its schema instead of creating a second type. The tenant could not be read in this session.
Creation-time required is true only for Status. Everything else can be completed after registration; the readiness list below says what must exist before an order.
Configure Category and Status as select fields with the option values exactly as listed; values are stable keys, labels can be translated.
Currency has no default: the country context is provisional. Set aoa as default only after confirming most suppliers invoice in Kz.
Payment-term options are illustrative company terms, not statutory. Replace with the organization's actual agreed terms.
Supplier code is a text field for the code assigned by the accounting/ERP system. Do not add an auto_number alongside it unless the organization has no external code at all (decision D3).

Manual-entry walkthrough: create «Demonstration Supplies, Lda.» knowing only trading name, category = goods, contact name/email and Status = prospective. Later: Purchasing adds NIF and address from the supplier's registration document, Finance supplies the accounting code once the supplier is created there, and payment terms/currency are filled after the first negotiation. Status moves to active when the organization decides the supplier may receive orders. NIF is entered in Provia and in accounting; the accounting system is authoritative and Purchasing copies it once (no synchronization).

Sensitivity: for a sole trader the NIF and phone are personal data. Restrict record access to Purchasing and Finance if the organization treats them as confidential; a sensitivity label is not permission enforcement.
readiness: Before an order is placed: Status = active, NIF, commercial email, currency and payment terms filled. The Status field does not block selection by itself; the order action's brief must instruct the assignee to check it.
Before invoice matching: accounting supplier code filled by Finance.

fields.label: Legal name
fields.helpText: Registered company name when it differs from the trading name used as the record Name.
fields.purpose: Identify the counterparty on orders and contracts when the trading name is not the registered name.

fields.label: NIF
fields.helpText: Tax identification number as shown on the supplier's document. Copied once from the accounting system, which stays authoritative.
fields.purpose: Match the supplier on orders and invoices and avoid duplicate records.
fields.sensitivity: Internal; personal data when the supplier is a sole trader

fields.label: Accounting supplier code
fields.helpText: Code assigned by the accounting/ERP system. Leave empty until Finance creates the supplier there.
fields.purpose: Reconcile Provia orders with accounting entries and invoices.

fields.label: Category
fields.helpText: What this supplier mainly provides. Used to filter suppliers when preparing a request and for spend reporting.
fields.purpose: Filter suppliers by what they provide and report spend by category.

fields.label: Commercial contact
fields.helpText: Person who answers requests for quotation and receives orders.
fields.purpose: Address quotations and orders to the right person.

fields.label: Commercial email
fields.helpText: Address to which requests for quotation and orders are sent.
fields.purpose: Send requests for quotation and orders.

fields.label: Commercial phone
fields.helpText: Phone for urgent coordination of deliveries.
fields.purpose: Reach the supplier when email is not enough.

fields.label: Address
fields.helpText: Address printed on the order or used for collection.
fields.purpose: Complete the order header and plan collections.

fields.label: Country
fields.helpText: Fill only for suppliers outside the organization's country; foreign suppliers usually change currency, lead time and payment terms.
fields.purpose: Recognise foreign suppliers when preparing the order and budget.

fields.label: Relationship owner
fields.helpText: Buyer who maintains this record and answers questions about the supplier.
fields.purpose: Know who keeps the record current and who to ask before an order.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Prospective: registered, not yet cleared for orders. Active: may receive orders. Suspended: no new orders until reviewed. Closed: relationship ended.
fields.purpose: Check before selecting the supplier on an order; filter active suppliers.

fields.label: Approved on
fields.helpText: Date the supplier was cleared to receive orders. Fill only if the organization runs a qualification step.
fields.purpose: Record when qualification happened for later review.

fields.label: Invoicing currency
fields.helpText: Currency in which this supplier quotes and invoices. Illustrative list; extend with the currencies actually used.
fields.purpose: Prepare the order and budget confirmation in the right currency.

fields.label: Payment terms
fields.helpText: Terms agreed with the supplier. Illustrative options; replace with the organization's actual terms.
fields.purpose: Carry agreed terms onto the order and inform Finance's budget confirmation.

fields.label: Typical lead time (days)
fields.helpText: Usual calendar days from order to delivery, as quoted or observed. Guidance only.
fields.purpose: Check whether the supplier can meet the request's needed-by date.

fields.label: Framework agreement
fields.helpText: Link to the signed framework contract or price list in the document repository, when one exists.
fields.purpose: Consult agreed prices and conditions before ordering.

fields.label: Agreement valid until
fields.helpText: End date of the framework agreement. Fill only when an agreement exists.
fields.purpose: Avoid ordering under an expired agreement and plan renewals.

fields.label: Notes
fields.helpText: Operational remarks useful to any buyer: delivery constraints, preferred ordering channel, known issues.
fields.purpose: Share supplier knowledge across buyers without re-asking.
fields.example: Delivers Tuesdays and Thursdays; orders by email only.

decisions.question: No purchasing procedure, sample supplier records or purchase-request examples were supplied. Which documents describe the current purchasing process, and which systems (accounting/ERP, document repository) hold supplier data today?
Who creates and maintains supplier records in Provia (assumed: Purchasing, with Finance filling the accounting code and confirming the NIF)?
Does the accounting/ERP system assign a supplier code? If yes, keep supplier_code as text; if no external code exists, replace it with a Provia auto_number (e.g. prefix SUP-).
Country of operation and default invoicing currency were not stated. Angola/AOA is a provisional context: confirm before setting a currency default or translating labels to pt-AO.

Is there a supplier qualification or evaluation cycle? If yes, confirm the approved_on field and add rating / last-evaluation fields with the evaluation process as maintainer; if no, drop approved_on.

Is a cost centre / department list needed on purchase requests for budget confirmation and reporting? If it is reused across purchasing, expenses and budgeting, it becomes a second entity type; otherwise a select on the case is enough.

Which approval steps and amount thresholds apply to a purchase request, and from which amount are quotations required? Needed before the purchase-request case fields (approved_amount, quotations) are configured in a workflow.
